title: Merry Making: Play, Build and Create With NVIDIA Technologies This Holiday Season
body: Merry Making: Play, Build and Create With NVIDIA Technologies This Holiday Season Get into the game, bring a creative project to life or try building a robot with NVIDIA platforms. November 23, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! The elves don’t have to be the only ones busy in the workshop this holiday season. With the lights twinkling and the gift wrap out, it’s the perfect time to give someone — or yourself — a spark to take a hobby to the next level. For some, that means diving into a new game. For others, it’s video editing or even building a robot. NVIDIA technologies offer something for everyone on Santa’s list. Read on to unwrap the details. Make Time for One More Game With the holiday break here, everyone can be online to score bragging rights or explore a world that’s only been seen in video game trailers. For some players, an upgrade means a desktop that brings out the detail in every scene. For others, it’s a laptop they can take along when visiting family, or a way to play in the cloud on a device they already own. The right setup depends on where and what to play: GeForce RTX 50 Series laptops and desktops power the action. Built on the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture, they feature fifth-generation Tensor Cores and fourth-generation RT Cores for AI-enhanced graphics, detailed ray-traced worlds and high frames-per-second gaming. NVIDIA RTX Spark PCs combine RTX graphics with NVIDIA’s full-stack AI platform on a single superchip, bringing decades of NVIDIA innovation to slim, premium laptops and compact desktops on the familiar Windows platform. One PC can handle every workflow, from accelerated creation and immersive gaming to powerful local AI  — with a variety of designs and all-day battery life. See games in a new light with NVIDIA DLSS 5 technology, which boosts performance and enhances image quality. The newest feature, DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, infuses scenes with lifelike lighting and materials in supported games. Get a glimpse of NBA 2K27 with DLSS 5 . NVIDIA Reflex and G-SYNC make gameplay more responsive and fluid. Reflex reduces system latency in supported games, while G-SYNC displays use variable refresh rates to deliver smooth, tear-free gaming. The GeForce NOW cloud gaming service enables playing top titles anywhere. Stream supported games on compatible laptops, TVs, handhelds and more. Connect to supported game stores to play owned PC games, with more than 4,500 titles available across the service. Make Something Worth Sharing For creators with a project that’s been on the backburner, the right gift this season can be the push to finally make it happen. Maybe it’s holiday clips becoming a short film, a snowy scene coming together in 3D or a livestream that brings friends across time zones to the same virtual table. Creators can use NVIDIA systems — such as GeForce RTX 50 Series and RTX Spark devices — to keep up with the workflows, along with NVIDIA Studio tools and technologies for AI acceleration. Studio Drivers support video editing, 3D design and livestreaming. In supported applications, faster processing gives more room to experiment and refine. Build a Robot That Thinks Every robot starts somewhere. This season, it could be under the tree. Building a robot is an experiment in teaching a device to see or sense its surroundings. A first project might be as simple as using a camera to identify a candy cane or a gingerbread man, then moving on to an app that probes what the camera sees. Testing brings new questions. Can the robot recognize the candy cane under twinkling lights? Can it tell a frosted gingerbread man from an unfrosted one? Each experiment leaves more to improve and explore. The NVIDIA Jetson edge AI platform provides the hardware and software to build projects like these. It combines compact computers with the NVIDIA JetPack software development kit to help makers build robots, autonomous machines and intelligent devices. A Jetson Developer Kit is a gift to explore computer vision, generative AI and multimodal robot control, with the option to add cameras and sensors suited to various projects. AI runs directly on the device, processing information from its surroundings. When ready to take a prototype further, production systems powered by Jetson modules provide a path to deployment. See how Microduck comes to life with NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super , bringing together robot movement, visual understanding and natural-language interaction. With Hermes Agent and NVIDIA Cosmos, developers can explore how AI connects everyday requests with actions in the physical world. Bring an SO-101 arm to life with NVIDIA Jetson Orin and explore agentic robotics. Give OpenClaw a simple request, and watch it plan the steps, call NVIDIA tools and check the results. OpenShell runs the agent securely in a sandbox, controlling its access to models and robot tools. Based on ASPIRE skills, the system reuses lessons from past attempts to guide future tasks. Build a robot companion that chats, moves and understands what it sees, with NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt and Cosmos open models running locally on Jetson Orin Nano 8GB. For more advanced projects, explore vision language action models and world action models to enable increasingly sophisticated robotic behaviors — beyond simple perception and predefined actions toward understanding natural language instructions, reasoning, planning multistep tasks and interacting with the physical world. Dive into setup guides and project tutorials in Jetson AI Lab . Whether it’s a gaming upgrade, a creative project or a first robot, the right tools can open up new possibilities well beyond the holidays. Explore NVIDIA’s holiday lineup for gamers, creators and makers. Categories: AI Gaming Hardware Robotics Software Tags: GeForce NOW GeForce RTX Jetson NVIDIA RTX NVIDIA Studio OpenShell Related News Supercomputing Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents Nov 17, 2026 Networking Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics Nov 16, 2026 AI Infrastructure NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing Nov 16, 2026 AI Infrastructure NVIDIA CUDA-X Libraries Give Agents the Tools to Accelerate Scientific Discovery Nov 16, 2026

title: Baltimore Recidivist Sex Offender Pleads Guilty to Child Sexual Abuse Material Possession
body: Press Release Baltimore Recidivist Sex Offender Pleads Guilty to Child Sexual Abuse Material Possession Monday, November 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maryland Baltimore, Maryland – A Baltimore recidivist sex offender pled guilty in federal court, today, to child sex-abuse crimes. Tarif Jahmil Alston, 43, pled guilty to possession of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) after authorities received a tip in connection with a CashApp transaction. Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the guilty plea with Special Agent in Charge Jimmy Paul, FBI Baltimore Field Office, and Commissioner Richard Worley, Baltimore Police Department (BPD). According to his guilty plea, between September 2025 and January 2026, Alston used his cellphone to send, receive, and collect CSAM. In October 2025, BPD received a CyberTip that linked a CSAM purchase to Alston’s CashApp account. Then on Jan. 28, 2026, law enforcement executed a search warrant at Alston’s Baltimore home. Law enforcement seized Alston’s cellphone and two laptops. A review of the cellphone revealed Alston used the BitComet application to download CSAM. At the time law enforcement seized the cellphone, CSAM was being actively downloaded within the application. Through a forensic analysis of the cellphone, law enforcement uncovered that Alston received more than 1,700 CSAM files. Additionally, Alston was previously convicted of second-degree sexual offense related to aggravated sexual abuse, sexual abuse, and abusive sexual contact involving a minor or ward.  Yet, Alston has not complied with his requirement to register as a sex offender since 2017. This case is part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse.  Led by the United States Attorney’s Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims.  For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit justice.gov/psc .  For more information about Internet safety education, please visit justice.gov/psc and click on the “Resources” tab on the left of the page. Alston faces a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years, with a maximum of 20 years in federal prison for possession of child sexual abuse material. Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. Sentencing is set for Thursday, Apr. 8, 2027, at 10:30 a.m. A federal district court judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the FBI and BPD for their work in the investigation. Ms. Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Colleen Elizabeth McGuinn and Elliott Higgins who are prosecuting the federal case. For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, visit justice.gov/usao-md . # # # Contact Kevin Nash USAMD.Press@usdoj.gov 410-209-4946 Updated November 23, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Maryland

title: Honduran Citizen and Convicted Felon Indicted for Illegal Re-entry
body: Press Release Honduran Citizen and Convicted Felon Indicted for Illegal Re-entry Monday, November 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS , LOUISIANA – On November 20, 2026 a federal grand jury indicted CESAR RICARDO VELASQUEZ BERNARDEZ a/k/a “CESAR VELASQUEZ,” a/k/a “RICARDO VELASQUEZ,” a/k/a “CESAR RICARDO VELASQUEZ,” a/k/a “CESAR RICARDO VELASQUEZ-BERNARDEZ,” a/k/a “CESAR VELASQUEZ-BERNARDEZ,” (“VELASQUEZ BERNARDEZ”) , age 43, a native of Honduras, for re-entry of a removed alien, in violation of Title 8, United States Code, Sections 1326(a) and (b)(1), announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle. According to the indictment, on or about November 3, 2026, in the Eastern District of Louisiana, VELASQUEZ BERNARDEZ , an alien, was found in the United States after having been deported and removed therefrom on or about October 23, 2020, without the approval of the Attorney General of the United States or his designated successor, the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, having expressly consented to the defendant’s reapplication for admission into the United States. VELASQUEZ BERNARDEZ faces a maximum term of imprisonment of ten (10) years, a fine of up to $250,000, up to three (3) years of supervised release, and a mandatory $100 special assessment cost. U.S. Attorney Courcelle reiterated that an indictment is merely a charge and that the guilt of the defendant must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt. U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of the United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Enforcement and Removal Operations (“ICE-ERO”) in investigating this matter.  Assistant United States Attorney Duane A. Evans of the General Crimes Unit is prosecuting the matter. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. *  *   * Contact Shane M. Jones Public Information Officer United States Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of Louisiana United States Department of Justice Updated November 23, 2026 Topic Operation Take Back America Component USAO - Louisiana, Eastern

title: Huntington Man Pleads Guilty to Federal Drug Crime
Prolific Child Molester and Self-Proclaimed “Elite Ranked Pedophile” Sentenced to 310 Years in Federal Prison
body: Press Release Prolific Child Molester and Self-Proclaimed “Elite Ranked Pedophile” Sentenced to 310 Years in Federal Prison Monday, November 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Jacksonville, Florida – Frederick Karl Hildenbrand (55, Cocoa) has been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Wendy Berger to 310 years in federal prison, followed by a lifetime of supervised release, for nine counts of production of child sex abuse material (CSAM) and two counts of possession of CSAM.  Hildenbrand was also ordered to pay $42,000 in restitution to the victims of some of the offenses. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. Hildenbrand was found guilty by a jury on May 20, 2026. According to evidence presented at trial, Hildenbrand was residing in Ohio from at least around 2004 through around 2014, when he and his wife relocated to northeast Florida. While in Ohio, Hildenbrand produced a number of videotapes and electronic files depicting himself sexually abusing children, including toddlers and infants. Hildenbrand brought these materials with him to Florida and in 2018 rented a storage unit in which he placed a safe containing CSAM. In May 2024, after the storage unit company had changed ownership, Hildenbrand’s payments were no longer processed, and the storage unit was auctioned. The purchaser of the contents retrieved a safe from the storage unit and, after opening it, discovered multiple pairs of soiled children’s panties labeled with names and individually packaged in plastic baggies. Also, inside the safe were videotapes and electronic devices. The purchaser turned the materials over to the Baker County Sheriff’s Office, and child exploitation material was discovered on multiple media. In July 2024, Hildenbrand realized that his unit had been auctioned and contacted the storage company to try and get his items returned. During multiple recorded phone calls, Hildenbrand expressed that he especially wanted the items returned from his safe. Unknown to Hildenbrand, he was having these conversations with an undercover detective from the Clay County Sheriff's Office. On August 5, 2024, Hildenbrand drove three hours from Cocoa to Clay County intending to get the safe back. Instead, he was arrested. On the same day, detectives searched Hildenbrand’s residence and recovered electronic devices, which also contained CSAM. Searches of these devices revealed that Hildenbrand had continued to film himself sexually abusing children through at least June 2024. In total, Hildenbrand possessed at least 10,000 depictions of children being sexually abused. One of his computers contained two versions of a “poem” written by Hildenbrand about his insatiable lust for children, in which he described himself as “an Elite ranked pedophile” for over 30 years. “Protecting our children from criminals is a high priority for our office,” said U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe. “Thanks to the relentless pursuit and diligence by our law enforcement partners, this sexual predator will finally face justice, and further victims will be saved from harm.” “A child was rescued from a child predator by HSI special agents and the Northeast Florida INTERCEPT Task Force as part of this investigation. This significant sentencing holds this criminal accountable for the lasting harm he inflicted on multiple child victims,” said Assistant Special Agent in Charge Timothy Hemker, HSI Jacksonville. “HSI remains committed and will use every available resource to protect children and bring those who commit these heinous offenses to justice.” This case was investigated by the Northeast Florida INTERCEPT Task Force, including Homeland Security Investigations, the Clay County Sheriff’s Office, the Cocoa Police Department, the Baker County Sheriff’s Office, and the Florida Department of Children and Families. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Laura Cofer Taylor. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov. Updated November 23, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Florida, Middle

title: Buffalo man pleads guilty to distributing fentanyl that caused the death of another individual
body: Press Release Buffalo man pleads guilty to distributing fentanyl that caused the death of another individual Monday, November 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of New York BUFFALO, NY—U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Kenneth G. Shoemaker, II a/k/a Kenny, 50, of Buffalo, NY, pleaded guilty before U.S. District Judge Lawrence J. Vilardo to distribution of fentanyl and maintaining a drug involved premises, which carry a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison and a $1,000,000 fine. Between January 2020, and February 7, 2025, Shoemaker sold large quantities of fentanyl, para-fluorofentanyl, crack cocaine, and amphetamine (Adderall), at his Sweet Avenue residence. He personally distributed the controlled substances on nearly a daily basis, accepting cash, Zelle, Cash App, stolen merchandise, such as shoes, clothing, and power tools, gift cards, social benefit program currency equivalents, such as EBT cards, and sex. Shoemaker also allowed customers to sign over benefit checks to him, including life insurance annuity payments. On the evening of September 23, 2023, Buffalo police responded to Shoemaker’s Sweet Avenue residence following a 911 call regarding an unresponsive male. Identified as E.I., he failed to respond to medical treatment on scene, and was taken to Buffalo General Hospital, where died a day later. E.I. was one of Showmaker’s regular drug customers. On September 22 and 23, 2023, the two exchanged text messages regarding E.I. purchasing controlled substances. Late in the morning on September 23, 2023, E.I. sent Shoemaker $200.00 via Cash App. In 2024, investigators conducted 12 controlled narcotics purchases from Shoemaker on twelve occasions, with each conducted directly from Shoemaker at his residence. In total, law enforcement purchased approximately $2,800 worth of controlled substances. During one of the controlled purchases, in July 2024, Shoemaker, while commenting on the strength of the fentanyl he supplied, stated that his fentanyl had caused the overdose death of an individual identified as E.I. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Louis A. Testani and Melanie J. Bailey. The plea is the result of an investigation by the Drug Enforcement Administration, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Farhana Islam, New York Field Division, the New York State Police, under the direction of Major Amie Feroleto, and the Buffalo Police Department, under the direction of Commissioner Erika Shields. Sentencing is scheduled for April 2, 2027, before Judge Vilardo. # # # # Contact Barbara Burns 716-843-5817 Updated November 23, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Opioids Component USAO - New York, Western

title: Felon Who Shot Man in 2018 Sentenced in D.C. After Fleeing Police With Loaded, High-Capacity Pistol
body: Press Release Felon Who Shot Man in 2018 Sentenced in D.C. After Fleeing Police With Loaded, High-Capacity Pistol Monday, November 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia WASHINGTON – Darious Phillips, 35, a previously convicted felon residing in the District of Columbia, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 20 months in prison in connection with his unlawful possession of a semiautomatic pistol while he was on supervised release for shooting a man three times, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. Phillips pleaded guilty on Nov. 6, 2025, before Judge Sparkle L. Sooknanan to one count of unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition by a felon. In addition to the 20-month prison sentence, Judge Sooknanan ordered Phillips to serve three years of supervised release. Federal prosecutors had requested a 41-month prison term. According to court papers, on Aug. 21, 2025, members of the Metropolitan Police Department’s Robbery Suppression Unit were patrolling the 4000 block of South Capitol Street SW when they saw Phillips walking with a woman. Phillips spotted the officers, pulled the woman closer to him, and pushed something into his jacket pocket before walking away at a faster pace. When officers approached him, Phillips dashed down a public sidewalk. As he ran, he pulled a loaded, semi-automatic pistol with an extended magazine from his jacket and threw it before officers caught up with him. Officers recovered a Masterpiece Arms Mac9 loaded with 19 rounds of 9mm ammunition along Phillips’s flight path minutes later. At the time of this offense, Phillips was on supervised release following a 2018 conviction for shooting a man three times outside a gas station. He had also been arrested less than a year earlier, in October 2024, after handing a loaded, unregistered “ghost gun” to the mother of his child moments before police stopped them near Mellon Street SE. The United States Parole Commission also ordered Phillips to serve a total of 36 months’ incarceration for violating the terms of his supervised release from the 2018 offense. Today’s sentence will run concurrently with the Parole Commission’s violation term of imprisonment. The investigation was conducted by the Metropolitan Police Department. The matter was prosecuted under the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful initiative by Assistant U.S. Attorney Mary Elizabeth Bultemeier. Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful is a law enforcement initiative in support of President Trump’s Executive Order to crack down on gun violence, prioritize federal firearms violations, pursue tougher penalties, and seek detention for federal firearms violators. title: Department of Justice Announces Nearly $150 Million to Hire Over 1,000 Law Enforcement Officers and Deputies
body: Press Release Department of Justice Announces Nearly $150 Million to Hire Over 1,000 Law Enforcement Officers and Deputies Monday, November 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Through the Office of Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS Office), the Department of Justice today announced it has awarded nearly $150 million under the 2026 COPS Hiring Program (CHP). CHP is a competitive grant program that provides funding directly to state, local, tribal, and territorial law enforcement agencies to pay for the entry-level salaries and fringe benefits of newly hired and rehired full-time sworn officers/deputies to make America safe again. CHP is a flagship program in the COPS Office, which has a long history of promoting police partnerships. Through CHP, this Administration supports our nation’s front-line heroes by providing them with needed resources and expertise to enhance policing strategies and tactics. The express purpose of CHP is crime reduction through effective common-sense policing. “Under the leadership of President Trump, violent crime has cratered to record lows,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “We were honored to host President Trump at the Department of Justice today to announce, among other actions, $150 million in grants for state and local law enforcement through the COPS Hiring Program. These funds will put more officers on the beat and keep the American people safe.” The CHP program focuses on advancing administration priorities. Funding was prioritized for agencies that focused on: Violent Crime, Squatting and Encampment Enforcement, Homeland and Border Security, Nuisance Abatement and Quality of Life, School-Based Policing, and Combating Domestic Terrorism. Additional priority consideration was given to agencies that commit to ending deadly sanctuary city polices, agencies that participate in the Homeland Security Task Force, and agencies that are within rural jurisdictions. Of the selected law enforcement agencies, one hundred and fifty-three recipients will use the funding to focus on violent crime, 40 will focus on school-based policing, 36 will seek to address nuisance abatement and quality of life, 17 will focus on other innovations in common sense policing, 16 will focus on homeland security and seven will focus on squatting and encampment enforcement. The demand for CHP funding remains extremely high among law enforcement agencies nationwide. The COPS Office received 551 requests for funding and was able to award 269 agencies, approximately 49%. More information on the 2026 CHP awards can be found here https://cops.usdoj.gov/chp-award . The COPS Office is the component of the U.S. Department of Justice responsible for advancing the practice of community policing and the Administration’s priority of Making America Safe Again by supporting the nation’s state, local, territorial, and Tribal law enforcement agencies through information and grant resources. To date, the COPS Office has been appropriated more than $21 billion to advance community policing including grants awarded to more than 13,000 state, local, and Tribal law enforcement agencies to fund the hiring and redeployment of more than 141,000 officers. Updated November 23, 2026 Topic Grants Components Office of the Attorney General Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) Press Release Number: 26-1403

title: 9 Illegal Aliens from Venezuela Sentenced for Roles in Nashville Sex Trafficking Organization as Part of Homeland Security Task Force Initiative
body: Press Release 9 Illegal Aliens from Venezuela Sentenced for Roles in Nashville Sex Trafficking Organization as Part of Homeland Security Task Force Initiative Monday, November 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs The last of nine illegal aliens from Venezuela were sentenced after they pleaded guilty to human trafficking and alien smuggling charges related to a sex trafficking ring that operated in several motels across Nashville, Tennessee. These defendants were sentenced in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee. “These sentences mark the final step in a relentless pursuit of justice against callous criminals who smuggled vulnerable victims across the border, then further exploited them via sex trafficking once they were in the United States, all to line their pockets,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Driven by greed, these nine illegal aliens turned human suffering into a business, treating the victims like commodities. Through the Homeland Security Task Force Initiative and Joint Task Force Alpha, we will dismantle these criminal networks, enforce our nation’s immigration laws, and ensure those who profit from human smuggling and trafficking are brought to justice.” “These defendants built a criminal enterprise on deception, fear, and the exploitation of vulnerable women right here in Nashville,” said U.S. Attorney Braden H. Boucek for the Middle District of Tennessee. “They sought to enrich themselves by stripping others of their freedom and dignity. Now, every member of this organization charged in this case has been held accountable. Those who seek to establish human trafficking networks in Middle Tennessee should know that we are committed not only to prosecuting their members, but to dismantling the criminal enterprises themselves.” “With lies and empty promises, the defendants used their roles in this criminal enterprise to exploit vulnerable people for profit” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Michael Perez of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Nashville. “The outcome of this Homeland Security Task Force investigation is a testament to the positive impact law enforcement can have when working in collaboration towards the common goal of holding criminals accountable. We are committed to the pursuit and dismantlement of these transnational criminal organizations.” “These sentences demonstrate the unwavering commitment of the Homeland Security Task Force to aggressively investigate, pursue, and prosecute those who orchestrate human smuggling and trafficking operations to prey on vulnerable women for profit,” said Special Agent in Charge Terence G. Reilly of the FBI Nashville Field Office. “We will leverage every available law enforcement resource to identify offenders, dismantle criminal networks, and hold those responsible accountable. No trafficker is beyond our reach, and no one is above the law.” “These sentences underscore the serious consequences facing those who use violence, threats, and coercion to profit from human trafficking and smuggling,” said Special Agent in Charge Donald “Trey” Eakins of IRS Criminal Investigation’s (IRS-CI) Charlotte Field Office. “We remain committed to working alongside our law enforcement partners to protect victims and disrupt the financial networks that support these crimes.” “These individuals crossed our borders to commit these heinous crimes as part of a much larger criminal organization. We have dealt that organization a significant blow, disrupted its criminal operations and, as a result, helped make our streets and neighborhoods safer,” said Director David Rausch of the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI). “Let this outcome send a clear message: If you come into our communities to exploit the vulnerable and profit from human suffering, we will find you and hold you accountable.” According to court documents, the defendants orchestrated a human trafficking and smuggling scheme targeting vulnerable Venezuelan women by recruiting them to the U.S. with promises of employment. After arranging and facilitating their travel to the U.S., the defendants directed the women to Nashville. Once there, these women were told they owed an inflated smuggling debt, which they could only repay through commercial sex work. Those who resisted faced threats of physical harm against themselves and their families. The defendants took a cut of the women’s earnings in addition to collecting on the inflated smuggling debts. Yilibeth Carmen Rivero-de Caldera (Rivero) and her son, Kleiver Daniel Mota Rivero (Mota), led and managed the human trafficking and smuggling scheme. Rivero enlisted her adult children and their spouses, Mota’s girlfriend, and others to take on various roles in the scheme. Rivero, Mota, and defendant Ramon De Jesus Velasquez Martinez (Velasquez) used threats of violence, including wielding firearms, to intimidate and force compliance from the women trafficked by the organization. To further intimidate the women, Mota and other defendants engaged in conduct that made the victims believe Mota was affiliated with a Venezuelan prison gang and openly spoke about Mota’s prior prison term for homicide in Venezuela. Rivero, Mota, Velasquez, and the six other defendants — Wilmarys Del Valle Manzano Solorzano, Endrik Alexander Morales-Rivero, Ariannys Beatriz Gutierrez-Carrillo, Frankyanna Del Valle Romero-Rivero, Jesus Enrique Castillo Rodriguez, and Yuribetzi Del Valle Gomez Machuca — arranged or otherwise aided the smuggling of the victims into the United States, posted online commercial sex advertisements for the victims, set up commercial sex appointments with men who responded to the postings, and collected the proceeds of the commercial sex acts. The court sentenced the nine defendants as follows: Yilibeth Carmen Rivero-de Caldera: 204 months in prison; Kleiver Daniel Mota Rivero: 204 months in prison; Ramon De Jesus Velasquez Martinez: 100 months in prison; Wilmarys Del Valle Manzano Solorzano: Time Served; Endrik Alexander Morales-Rivero: 66 months in prison; Ariannys Beatriz Gutierrez-Carrillo: 50 months in prison; Frankyanna Del Valle Romero-Rivero: 50 months in prison; Jesus Enrique Castillo Rodriguez: 48 months in prison; and Yuribetzi Del Valle Gomez Machuca: 60 months. In addition to the sentences imposed above, the court ordered that Rivero and Mota pay a total of $171,614 in restitution to four identified victims. The court further ordered that several of the other defendants were jointly and severally liable with Rivero and Mota for various portions of the total restitution order depending on their conduct toward individual victims. Trial Attorneys Lindsey Roberson, Jessica Arco, and Alexandra Skinnion of the Criminal Division’s Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section (HRSP) and Assistant U.S. Attorney Katy Risinger for the Middle District of Tennessee are prosecuting the case. These prosecutions are part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole- of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. The Nashville HSTF comprises agents and officers from his, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives (ATF), the FBI, IRS-CI, U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS), U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), U.S. Secret Service (USSS), Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), and other federal agencies, working in collaboration with our state and local partners, with the prosecutions being led by the Middle District of Tennessee. This case was further supported and prosecuted by Joint Task Force Alpha (JTFA), the U.S. Department of Justice’s lead effort in combating human smuggling and trafficking committed by cartels and Transnational Criminal Organizations throughout the Americas. In partnership with the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), JTFA investigates and prosecutes the most prolific and dangerous human smuggling and trafficking networks that impact public safety and border security. Led by HRSP and supported by other Criminal Division components, JTFA has dedicated prosecutors from U.S. Attorneys’ Offices along the Southwest border, Southern Florida, Northern New York, and Vermont. JTFA partners with U.S. Attorneys’ Offices throughout the country and supports high-priority cases in any district. All JTFA cases rely on substantial law enforcement resources from DHS components, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, HSI, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Border Patrol, and the Office of Field Operations. JTFA also partners with FBI and other law enforcement agencies. To date, JTFA’s work has resulted in more than 486 domestic and international arrests of leaders, organizers, and significant facilitators of alien smuggling and trafficking; more than 447 U.S. convictions; and more than 374 significant jail sentences imposed and forfeitures of substantial assets. Anyone who has information about human trafficking should report that information to the National Human Trafficking Hotline toll-free at 1-888-373-7888, which is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. For more information about human trafficking, please visit www.humantraffickinghotline.org . Information on the Justice Department’s efforts to combat human trafficking can be found at www.justice.gov/humantrafficking . body: Press Release Tampa Man Sentenced to Over Twelve Years for Robbing Gas Station and Discharging Firearm Monday, November 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Tampa, FL - Rafael Jimenez (31, Tampa) has been sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Virginia M. Hernandez Covington to over 12 years and 3 months in federal prison, followed by 3 years of supervised release, for robbing a Tampa gas station and discharging a firearm during the robbery. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court records, on March 8, 2025, Jimenez entered a gas station in Tampa and brandished a firearm while demanding money from the register. Shortly after making this demand, Jimenez fired a shot in the direction of the clerk, striking the ground directly behind the clerk. Jimenez stole over $600 from the store as well as cigarettes. He was apprehended after surveillance footage from days before the robbery showed physical similarities between Jimenez and the robber, including a distinctive tattoo. Evidence found in Jimenez’s trash outside his home included a ski mask, gloves, and cigarettes of the same brand the robber used. Surveillance video from nearby businesses showed a vehicle similar to Jimenez’s traveling on roads close to the scene of the robbery before and after it occurred. This case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Samantha Newman. Assistant United States Attorney Suzanne Nebesky is handling the forfeiture. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Active-Duty U.S. Army Sergeant Pleads Guilty in Conspiracy to Gather and Transfer National Defense Information
body: Press Release Active-Duty U.S. Army Sergeant Pleads Guilty in Conspiracy to Gather and Transfer National Defense Information Monday, November 23, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Oregon PORTLAND, Ore. — Jian Zhao, 37, an active-duty U.S. Army sergeant stationed at Joint Base Lewis-McChord in Washington, pleaded guilty to conspiring to gather, transmit and transfer national defense information to individuals connected to China, U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford announced today. The charge carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in federal prison, a $250,000 fine, up to three years of supervised release and a $100 special assessment. “Members of the United States military are entrusted with protecting some of our nation’s most sensitive information and capabilities,” said U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford. “The defendant violated that trust by exploiting his access to military information and equipment for personal profit while knowingly providing materials to individuals linked to China. Protecting our national security depends on holding accountable those who compromise their oath and endanger the security of our armed forces.” “This guilty plea reflects a deliberate betrayal of the oath every Soldier takes to defend our nation and safeguard our fellow service members,” said Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, the commanding general of Army Counterintelligence Command . “By trading access to sensitive military information and government equipment for personal profit, this individual undermined our Army’s operational security and put Soldiers at risk. I urge everyone across our ranks to stay vigilant and report any suspicious activity or outreach to Army Counterintelligence.” “The integrity of our national security depends, in part, on the trust placed in individuals granted access to classified information,” said FBI Portland Special Agent in Charge Doug Olson. “By pleading guilty, Jian Zhao has admitted to betraying that trust and abusing the responsibilities that came with his position and security clearance. Those who choose to compromise sensitive military information for personal gain put our nation's interests at risk, and the FBI, alongside our law enforcement and military partners, remains committed to holding them accountable.” According to court documents, Zhao enlisted in the U.S. Army in 2017 and served as a battery supply sergeant. As part of his duties, Zhao maintained a security clearance and had authorized access to sensitive military information and equipment. Federal investigators determined that, beginning around November 2021 and continuing through March 2025, Zhao conspired with Ruoyu Duan, a former U.S. Army soldier living in Hillsboro, Oregon, and others to obtain and transfer information and equipment related to the national defense to buyers in China. Duan, who previously pleaded guilty to conspiracy to transmit national defense information, recruited active-duty U.S. military personnel, including Zhao, to provide defense-related information and facilitated communications and financial transactions with China-based purchasers. As part of the conspiracy, Zhao provided excerpts from technical manuals related to the High Mobility Artillery Rocket System, offered military computers and government hard drives for sale and photographed restricted military presentations and documents concerning U.S. Army operations, communications networks, rocket and missile systems and military exercises. Zhao also sold military materials he described as sensitive, secret, or top secret and received thousands of dollars in payments from overseas buyers. He also removed government property and military storage devices without authorization and photographed controlled military documents using his personal cell phone. On March 6, 2025, federal agents arrested Zhao at his residence in Lacey, Washington, where they recovered approximately $30,000 in cash, electronic devices and multiple Army hard drives. Under the terms of the plea agreement, Zhao agreed to forfeit $17,500 as proceeds of the offense and abandon his interest in approximately $30,000 seized during the investigation. Zhao is scheduled to be sentenced on March 1, 2027. This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, with assistance from the U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command and other federal partners. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Geoffrey A. Barrow and Katherine Rykken for the District of Oregon and Trial Attorneys Yifei Zheng and Christopher Magnani of the Department of Justice's National Security Division are prosecuting the case. ### Updated November 23, 2026 Component USAO - Oregon
